summary: Arthur Venis was an Indologist who studied at Balliol College (~1874–1878). He served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1888–1914) and taught James Haughton Woods.

Arthur W. Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1894–1898) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and at Leipzig University (~1898–1901) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught at Harvard (~1902–1906) and the University of California (~1906–1938).

Arthur Waley was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at King's College (~1907–1910) and under Gustav Haloun (~1938–1951), and held posts at the British Museum (1913) and SOAS University of London.

Aruna Haldar worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Calcutta (~1936–1942) under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedar Nath Ojha, and later taught at Patna University (~1946–1968).

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist who studied under M. V. Upadhyay and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt (~1946–1953). He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Baroda College (~1951–1959).

Arvind Sharma works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1974–1978). He held posts at Queensland, Harvard (~2003–2004), and McGill (Birks Chair, ~1987).

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Until around 2009, he served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy and Head of Buddhist Thought at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya.
Asatoshi Kamiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an M.A. at Komazawa University. He worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School.
Asef Bayat studied at the University of Kent (~1980–1984). He held posts at Leiden University (2000–2010) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2010).
Asen Balikci studied at Columbia University (~1957–1962) and held an academic post at the Université de Montréal (~1961–1994).

Ashby Butnor specializes in philosophy and Japanology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Hawaii (~2003–2009) under Vrinda Dalmiya and served as a Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver.

Ashok Aklujkar specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1965–1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held a post at the University of British Columbia (~1969–2006).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1967). He founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.
Ashok Vajpeyi is a scholar associated with Indology. He completed his M.A. studies at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (~1961–1963).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee (-1967), and held posts as lecturer at Jangipur College and Senior Research Fellow at Calcutta.

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), Academy of Finland (1982–1990), and University of Helsinki (1981–2005).

Asutosh Mookerjee was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he later served as President (1906–1923), and held a post at Calcutta High Court (1904).
Atsuhiko Yoshida is a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Seikei University and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957), and held a post at Seikei University (~1977–1990).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989). He held a post as professor at Toyo University (~2007).

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1980) under Katsuhiko Kamimura, and held posts at the Meteorological College and Komazawa University (~1993–2002).
